era: The Merchant Who Kept Giving It Away
teaser: Offered half a man's wealth and one of his wives, he answered: 'Show me the market.'
quran_mention: When he collapsed, his wife Umm Kulthum went out to the mosque acting on «وَاسْتَعِينُوا بِالصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَاةِ» — 'and seek help through patience and prayer' (2:45).

layers.title: Who He Was
layers.subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ gave him a new name
layers.content:
He was Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf ibn Abd Awf ibn Abd ibn al-Harith ibn Zuhra ibn Kilab — Banu Zuhra, the clan of the Prophet's ﷺ own mother. His kunya was Abu Muhammad. His mother was ash-Shifa bint Awf. He was born ten years after the Year of the Elephant, which made him about ten years younger than the Prophet ﷺ.

He did not start with that name. In the Jahiliyyah he was called Abd Amr; one report has it as Abd al-Ka'ba, servant of the Ka'bah. The Prophet ﷺ renamed him Abd ar-Rahman, servant of the Merciful, when he became Muslim. It is worth pausing on: a man whose name had pointed at a building was turned to point at Allah.

Ya'qub ibn Utba described him as a tall man with a handsome face and fine skin, white with a tinge of red, and a back that bent with age. He never dyed his hair or his beard when they went white.

One small exchange survives about his caution. The Prophet ﷺ asked him what he did when greeting the Black Stone. 'All I did was greet it and move on,' he said. 'You were correct,' the Prophet ﷺ told him.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Conversion
layers.subtitle: In before Islam had a house to meet in
layers.content:
Yazid ibn Ruman gives the timing precisely: Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf became Muslim before the Prophet ﷺ had entered the house of al-Arqam ibn al-Arqam, and before he had begun calling people to Islam there. That house was Islam's first meeting place. He was already inside the religion when it still had nowhere to gather.

What it cost him is measured in journeys. He emigrated to Abyssinia, and Ibn Ishaq and al-Waqidi both say he went on both migrations — twice out of Arabia, and then a third time out of Makkah to Madinah.

Uthman ibn Affan later settled the question of his rank in a sentence. He was riding with a group and saw a man ahead in a black wrap and asked who it was. Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf, they told him. Uthman called al-Miswar ibn Makhrama over and said: if anyone claims he is better than your uncle in the first and the second emigration, he has lied.

He is also named by al-Mubarakpuri among the eight who formed the front line of the new faith in Arabia — the ones who had no crowd to stand in.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III; al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar

layers.title: With the Prophet ﷺ
layers.subtitle: 'Show me the market' — a fortune from nothing
layers.content:
He arrived in Madinah with nothing. The Prophet ﷺ joined him in brotherhood to Sa'd ibn ar-Rabi' of the Ansar, and Sa'd made him an offer that no one would blame him for taking: I am the wealthiest man in Madinah. Take half my property. I have two wives — choose one and I will divorce her for you.

Abd ar-Rahman's answer was: may Allah bless you in your wealth and your family. Show me the market.

They showed him. He bought and sold and came back the same day with a profit — a skin of ghee and some curd. Not long after he turned up with the trace of saffron on him. Married, he explained. What was her dower, asked the Prophet ﷺ. The weight of a date-kernel in gold. 'Then hold a wedding feast, even if it is one sheep.' Of himself he said: I think if I lifted a stone I would expect to find gold or silver under it.

He fought at Badr, Uhud and the Ditch, and he held his ground at Uhud when the army turned back. On the Tabuk expedition the Prophet ﷺ was delayed and came to find Abd ar-Rahman already leading the prayer — and prayed behind him rather than interrupt.
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet ﷺ after praying behind him at Tabuk: 'A Prophet has never been taken until he has prayed behind a righteous man of his community' — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Reported from Anas ibn Malik and from al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III

layers.title: The Trial
layers.subtitle: His test was the thing everyone else wanted
layers.content:
His trial was not poverty. It was success, and he knew it.

The Prophet ﷺ said to him: Ibn Awf, you are one of the wealthy, and you will enter the Garden only in a crowd — so lend to Allah and He will free your feet. What should I lend, Messenger of Allah? 'Begin with how you spend your evening.' All of it? 'Yes.' Abd ar-Rahman left worried. Then the Prophet ﷺ sent after him with an easing: Jibril says, command Ibn Awf to give hospitality to guests, feed the poor, give to those who ask, and start with the people he already supports. When he does that, it is a purification of what he is in.

There is a scene that shows the weight of it. A caravan of his came into Madinah and the city was in uproar. Aisha asked what the noise was, and was told: the caravan of Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf. Five hundred camels. She said she had heard the Prophet ﷺ describe Abd ar-Rahman on a path, leaning off it at times and straightening at others, and only just getting through.

When the report reached him he did not argue with it. He knew what a caravan of five hundred camels does to a man's chances.
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet ﷺ: 'Ibn Awf, you are one of the wealthy... so lend to Allah and He will release your feet for you' — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: Forty thousand dinars, handed straight out
layers.content:
He answered the warning with his ledger. He sold his land at Kaydama, his share of the property of Banu an-Nadir, for forty thousand dinars, and divided the whole sum among the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. When al-Miswar carried Aisha her portion she asked who had sent it, and on hearing the name she said the Prophet ﷺ had told his wives that no one would be kind to them after him except the steadfast — and had prayed that Ibn Awf be given to drink from the Salsabil of the Garden.

Umar named him to the council of six that would choose the next caliph. Amr ibn al-As suspected he wanted the office himself. Told of it, Abd ar-Rahman said he would sooner have a knife put to his throat and run through. He then asked the others to let him choose on their behalf, and Ali answered: yes, I am the first to be pleased.

He died in 32 AH, aged seventy-five. Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas took the bier on his own back saying, 'O our great mountain.' He left fifty thousand dinars bequeathed in the way of Allah, and gold that had to be broken up with axes until the men's hands blistered.
layers.hadith_ref: Umm Salama: the Prophet ﷺ said to his wives, 'The one who will protect you after me is the truthful pious one. O Allah, let Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf drink from the Salsabil of the Garden' — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

quiz.prompt: Sa'd ibn ar-Rabi' offered his new brother half his property and one of his two wives. What did Abd ar-Rahman ask for instead?

options.text: A loan he could repay with interest-free trade
Directions to the market
A plot of land beside the mosque
Nothing at all, and he moved to another house

quiz.citation: Reported from Anas ibn Malik — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He blessed the offer and declined it in the same breath. By the end of that first day he had traded his way to a skin of ghee and some curd — the first profit of the largest fortune among the Muhajirun.

quiz.prompt: What was Abd ar-Rahman called before Islam?

options.text: Abd Amr, and in one report Abd al-Ka'ba
Abd al-Uzza
Awf ibn al-Harith
Abu Muhammad az-Zuhri

quiz.citation: Reported from Amr ibn Dinar and from Ibn Sa'd — Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Prophet ﷺ renamed him Abd ar-Rahman — servant of the Merciful. A name that had pointed at a place was turned to point at Allah.

quiz.prompt: What did the Prophet ﷺ warn Abd ar-Rahman about, given his wealth?

options.text: That trade would keep him from the mosque
That his sons would quarrel over the inheritance
That he would enter the Garden only in a crowd, and should lend to Allah so his feet would be freed
That the Ansar would resent him

quiz.citation: Reported from Ibrahim ibn Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf from his father — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He asked how much he should give and was told to start with the evening's expenditure. When he asked whether he should give all of it, the answer was yes — and it frightened him. The easing came afterwards, through Jibril.

quiz.prompt: What did Abd ar-Rahman do with the forty thousand dinars he raised from selling his land?

options.text: Equipped an army for Syria
Distributed it — to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, and in another report also to the poor of Banu Zuhra and the needy
Bought the caravan of five hundred camels
Placed it in the treasury at Madinah

quiz.citation: Reported from al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and from the children of Abd ar-Rahman — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Aisha's response was to recall the Prophet's ﷺ words that only the steadfast would be kind to his wives after him, and his du'a that Ibn Awf drink from the Salsabil of the Garden.

quiz.prompt: Umar placed him on the council of six to choose the next caliph. How did Abd ar-Rahman treat the possibility of being chosen himself?

options.text: He accepted it as a duty he could not refuse
He said he would sooner have a knife put to his throat and run through
He left Madinah until the matter was settled
He asked for it openly, on the grounds of seniority

quiz.citation: Reported from Umm Bakr bint al-Miswar from her father — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Having removed himself, he asked the rest to let him decide for them, and Ali said he was the first to be pleased with that. The man they trusted to choose was the one who did not want it.

quiz.prompt: Abd ar-Rahman turned down half a fortune and asked for a market instead. Which part of that is hardest for you?

options.text: Refusing generosity without insulting the giver
Believing I could rebuild from nothing
Choosing effort when ease is genuinely on offer
None of it — I would rather owe nobody anything

quiz.citation: Reflection on the account of Sa'd ibn ar-Rabi' and Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Notice he did not lecture Sa'd about self-reliance. He made du'a for him first and asked for directions second.

quiz.prompt: The Prophet ﷺ told him his wealth would slow him down. If someone said that to you about the thing you are building, how would you take it?

options.text: I would take it seriously and change something
I would agree in principle and carry on unchanged
I would look for the reading of it that lets me keep going
I would want to know exactly what to do instead

quiz.citation: Reflection on the Prophet's ﷺ words to Ibn Awf — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: His first reaction was worry, not defence. The instruction that followed was practical: guests, the poor, those who ask, and your own dependants first.

quiz.prompt: Aisha heard five hundred camels arriving and remembered a warning rather than admiring the wealth. What does the sound of someone else's success do to you?

options.text: I feel behind
I feel glad for them and unbothered
I wonder what it is costing them
I mostly do not notice

quiz.citation: Reported from Habib ibn Abi Marzuq — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Her thought was not envy and not admiration. It was concern for him — the reaction of someone who had understood what the Prophet ﷺ said about the rich.

quiz.prompt: He gave away sums that would have made a dynasty, and still died leaving gold that had to be split with axes. How do you judge partial detachment?

options.text: Giving a great deal while keeping a great deal is still giving
What counts is the proportion, not the amount
What counts is whether the keeping made me anxious
I am not in a position to grade anyone on this

quiz.citation: Reflection on the estate of Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: The sources record both facts without embarrassment: the enormous giving and the enormous estate. They let the tension stand.

quiz.prompt: He said he would rather have his throat cut than be suspected of wanting authority. What is your relationship with being in charge?

options.text: I want it and I say so
I want it and would rather nobody noticed
I avoid it and sometimes that is cowardice
I take it when it is put on me and never seek it

quiz.citation: Reflection on the shura of six — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He removed himself from the running and then took on the harder job: making the choice and answering for it. Refusing power is not the same as refusing responsibility.
